title: Quarterly ops roadmap: Autoscale experiments & reservation testbed (Q2 pilot)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Run a focused quarter-long program to validate autoscale strategies on Dedicated pools and quantify reservation utilization trade-offs. We will run three parallel experiments in Q2: (1) predictive surge autoscale (learned traffic models + proactive allocation), (2) aggressive burst policy with short-lived reservations for tail loads, and (3) conservative autoscale with strict SLO-first fallbacks. The program will produce a runbook for production rollout, a set of guardrails for billing and SLA exposure, and a dashboard to track unit economics. Deliverables: experiment design docs, telemetry dashboards, cost/SLO analysis, updated rollout playbook, and a recommended default autoscale policy for tiered customers.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment 1 (predictive): demonstrate >=10% reduction in token cost for steady workloads without >2% degradation in p50/p95 latency
Experiment 2 (burst): show ability to absorb 3x sudden QPS spikes for up to 10 minutes with fallback policies exercised and no customer-visible errors
Experiment 3 (conservative): maintain SLOs while improving reservation utilization by >=8% compared to baseline
Runbook and guardrails published in Confluence and referenced from Console ops page
Grafana dashboard with cost, reservation utilization, SLOs, and per-pool autoscale actions available to oncall and product owners
Customer-facing FAQ + billing impact summary drafted for enterprise accounts

decisions: Run three smaller experiments in parallel rather than one large pilot to accelerate learnings and reduce blast radius.
Prioritize building a single observability dashboard that combines cost, utilization, and SLOs to avoid fragmentation across teams.
Use short-lived reservations (<=1 hour) only for Experiment 2 to contain billing exposure; require automated undo path if overbudget triggers fire.
Keep default production policy conservative for GA; present aggressive and predictive policies as opt-in advanced settings for Dedicated customers.
risks: Over-optimizing for cost could increase p95 latency for tail workloads — mitigation: strict rollback thresholds and circuit-breaker on SLO violation.
Billing surprises for enterprise customers if burst reservations are not properly surfaced — mitigation: billing simulator and opt-in checkbox.
Telemetry gaps: need kernel-level scheduling and KV cache hit metrics (dependency ENG-2715).
Operational complexity: new autoscale policies add cognitive load to oncall — mitigation: automation + clear runbook steps.
metrics: Unit cost per 1k tokens (baseline and experiment delta)
SLO hit rate (p50/p95 latency, error rate)
Autoscale action frequency and mean time to stabilize after scale events
Billing variance for sample enterprise accounts (simulated)
